THE MUSIC_GRAPH FEEDBACK FILE IS FOUR SESSIONS APPENDED, AND ITS FIRST BATCH WAS FIXED TWO WEEKS AGO. A standing hand-off note has been sending sessions after solved problems.

THE FILE'S OWN HEADER SAYS SO and nobody had read it: "reflow2 feedback — from an /adopt pass over music_graph / reflow2 0.20.0, 2026-08-01". The current version is 0.32.1 — twelve minor versions later. The file is not one report; it is FOUR sessions appended under one name:
  §1 F1–F9, W1–W7   — the 0.20.0 adopt pass, 2026-08-01
  §2 F5-again, F10–F16, W8–W10
  §3 F17–F22, W11–W15
  §4 F23–F24, W16      — triaged 2026-08-16 (PR #200, PR #205)

⭐ VERIFIED FIXED, EACH AGAINST THE RUNNING CODE RATHER THAN THE CHANGELOG:
• F5 ("Interface modelling silently manufactures circular dependencies", the reporter's own DANGEROUS tag, and the item the hand-off named as the thing to do FIRST) — FIXED 2026-08-01 in PR #19, with F5(b) following in PR #23. Reproduced music_graph's exact case in a throwaway test (two components, two `medium: data` interfaces, each providing what the other consumes). The finding now reads: "circular dependency: … every hop is a contract VIA ifc:midi-file, ifc:wav-audio, and EVERY ONE is a library/data medium — something read or linked against, not called across at run time … No DEPENDS_ON edge is involved", at severity WARNING rather than CRITICAL. Both of the reporter's asks are met: (a) the shared interfaces are named, (b) the severity is downgraded.
• F3 ("`designation: required` does not suppress unprovided_interface") — FIXED 2026-08-09, `detect.rs:1843`: a `required` boundary is skipped outright. Note it was fixed for a DIFFERENT trigger (`dec:linked-repos-poc` producing nine such gaps), not from this report — the report was never the reason, but the effect closes it.
• F4 ("orphan_node counts only REALIZES") — FIXED, `heal.rs:830-872`: now REALIZES / DOCUMENTS / SPECIFIES / PRODUCES / SATISFIES, with a comment recording that it used to be REALIZES alone.

⚠️ THE COST OF THE ERROR, stated plainly because it is the transferable part: the hand-off note carried "music_graph F1–F24 UNTRIAGED" for roughly two weeks and ranked F5 FIRST on the strength of the reporter's "(dangerous)" tag. A session acting on that would have spent itself re-fixing three solved defects. The tag was real and the priority reasoning was sound — the failure was never checking the report against the build, which is this project's own standing rule applied to feedback and not applied to the to-do list ABOUT feedback.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY STILL OPEN, and this is now the honest list: §2 and §3 — F10 through F22, minus F21 and F22, which were closed 2026-08-16 (the stale-status detector and the measurement-date work). NOT YET VERIFIED one way or the other: F6, F7, F8, F9 from §1 — the same triage pass covered them, so they are more likely fixed than not, but nobody has checked.

THE RULE THIS YIELDS: a feedback file states the VERSION it was written against. Read that line before ranking anything in it, and re-verify every item against the current build before believing a to-do list about it — including one written by a previous session of yourself.
